meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'A good PR story is infinitely more effective than a front page ad'?
meta.ogDescription: Probably his — but nobody who quotes it says where he said it, and the one Virgin page cited does not carry it.

answer.label: Attributed to
answer.authorDates: b. 1950 · English entrepreneur, founder of the Virgin Group
answer.sourceLine: Branson is credited with this wherever it appears, and nothing contradicts it. But nobody who quotes it says where he said it. Wikiquote traces it no further than “Mr. Branson’s blog on the Virgin Website” — no link, no date, no post title — and that post could not be opened from here to confirm the wording.

source.heading: The source

docMeta.dd: a post on Branson’s Virgin.com blog — no URL, no date

source.excerpt: “A good PR story is infinitely more effective than a front page ad.”
trail: Wikiquote lists the line on its Richard Branson page ↗, sourced only as “From Mr. Branson’s blog on the Virgin Website” — no link, no date, no post title.

The obvious candidate does not hold it. Wikiquote’s own external links point to Virgin.com’s “Richard Branson’s top 20 Virgin inspirational insights.” We read the archived copy from May 2013 ↗: it carries twenty Branson quotations, and this is not one of them.

What we could not do. virgin.com itself is unreachable from the environment this page was built in, so Branson’s blog archive has not been searched post by post. The attribution is credible and undocumented, not settled.
source.excerptNote: We would normally print the sentence inside the paragraph it came from. There is no paragraph to print: every version we could reach carries the line on its own, with nothing around it.
source.rightsNote: Whatever the source turns out to be, it is modern: Branson was born in 1950, and nothing he has written or said is anywhere near the public domain. Because we have not identified the publication that first carried the line, we name him as the speaker rather than asserting which publisher holds the text.

author.bio: Sir Richard Charles Nicholas Branson was born in Blackheath, London, in 1950, is dyslexic, and left Stowe School at sixteen to start a magazine called Student. A mail-order record business followed in 1970 and the first Virgin Records shop in 1972; the brand later carried an airline, a rail franchise and a spaceflight company. He was knighted in 2000 for services to entrepreneurship.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote's Richard Branson page lists “A good PR story is infinitely more effective than a front page ad.” with the sole source note “From Mr. Branson's blog on the Virgin Website.”
The archived May 2013 copy of Virgin.com's “Richard Branson's top 20 Virgin inspirational insights” does NOT contain this line; it carries twenty other Branson quotations.
Wikipedia gives Branson's birth as 18 July 1950 in Blackheath, London, his first venture as Student magazine at sixteen, Virgin Records from 1972, and a knighthood in 2000.
